findings.text: "The change is a substitution, not a behaviour change" is falsified by the run's own instrument: my 16-input probe of two scratch trees differing only in reckon/crew/recovery.py (base blob 860548cae, head blob 00332d4fd) moves 11 of 96 cells - padded and lowercase-z stamps newly parse in _budget_timing, _attempt_started_seconds, _seconds_since_dispatch, _worker_launched_after_manifest and _manifest_wait - and the recorded six-input table carries neither shape, so a reader of the fragment alone concludes that no behaviour moved.

the neutral verdict is not preserved for stamps the base revision could not read: with created_at " 2026-09-29T01:02:03Z " or "2026-09-29T01:02:03z" the base revision returned budget_seconds None, elapsed_seconds None and budget_overrun False, while head returns budget_seconds 3600, elapsed_seconds 82677 and budget_overrun True (overrun 79077); :3742 _seconds_since_dispatch returns 82677.0 where base returned None, against its own docstring that a run whose time cannot be read has taken no measurement; :3086 _worker_launched_after_manifest flips False to True; and :3424 _manifest_wait's age moves off the file mtime onto the parsed stamp - the widening is defensible in direction (it also removes the internal disagreement where started_at displayed a raw stamp while age_seconds came from the file mtime) but it is recorded nowhere.

the head arm's second revision line names the base sha 25dabb312d926dfc7081e887f9628e51a45062ce, so the log identifies the head content by no revision at all; the arm was written at 22:12 and the commit was made at 22:21:41, so the gate measured a working tree, and the manifest's after_suite.revision 2335dd269 is a claim the log cannot support - the corroboration that the gated bytes are the committed ones is indirect: head exceeds base by exactly 39 passes, the new test's own count, all of them in that file.

item_verdicts.done_when: the fence's clauses hold under my own reading - no fromisoformat remains in reckon/crew/recovery.py (0 by my AST scan and by grep), tests/test_recovery_timestamps_reuse_the_parser.py holds the per-reader table over the six named inputs with values taken from the shared parser's base revision (its EXPECTED literal is equal to the run's own base-table.json, whose stderr names /tmp/base-recov45UZ/reckon/crew/recovery.py), the table passes 39/39 in my own run at the head tree, the diff's nine hunks are the import line plus the six named functions and nothing else, both arm logs carry the seven tests/ files my AST scan independently finds importing reckon.crew.recovery at both revisions, both logs end with an EXIT= line, both basetemps are deleted, and the head adds no failing test id (17 failed / 247 passed base against 17 failed / 286 passed head, the failing-id sets identical by cmp); the one clause it does not meet is that the head arm's own header names the base revision (FINDING).
item_verdicts.goal: the node's goal is the six timestamp readers in reckon/crew/recovery.py resolving their stamps through reckon._timestamps.parse_utc while each keeps its own coercion and naive-as-UTC rule; all six now call it (seven call sites at :1537/:1564, :3086, :3236, :3424, :3569, :3742) and my AST scan finds no datetime.fromisoformat call left in the module, but my 16-input probe of two scratch trees differing only in recovery.py (base blob 860548cae, head blob 00332d4fd) moves 11 of 96 cells, so a reader does not keep its own acceptance set (FINDING).
item_verdicts.manifest: read; every key is filled, the logs it names exist and carry what it states (base-arm.log 17 failed / 247 passed EXIT=1, head-arm.log 17 failed / 286 passed EXIT=1, negative-control.log 1 failed / 38 passed with the declared string verbatim on its first line), baseline_suite and after_suite are complete JSON whose commands carry the real file lists after the run's own declared placeholder substitution, measurement_module and measurement_cwd name the base scratch tree, and failure_attribution is empty consistent with zero added failures; the head arm's log header records the base revision, so after_suite.revision rests on the commit rather than on the log (FINDING).
item_verdicts.write_paths: the two commits touch exactly the three declared paths - reckon/crew/recovery.py, tests/test_recovery_timestamps_reuse_the_parser.py and docs/evidence/fragments/a-worker-reuses-before-it-writes/recovery-timestamps-reuse-the-parser.html - the declared figures directory is unused, the worktree is clean at e455cc075, and within the module nothing outside the import line and the six named functions is amended.

justifications.durability: the table at tests/test_recovery_timestamps_reuse_the_parser.py asserts literals recorded from the base revision, so reverting any reader reddens it - my own mutation (reading the wall clock as UTC in _attempt_started_seconds, verified to move the offset cell from 1790636578.0 to 1790643778.0 before I drew any conclusion) failed the offset row and, because it reintroduced a fromisoformat call, the AST guard as well - but the table's input list omits the padded and lowercase-z shapes whose behaviour moved.
justifications.evidence: the gate measures the fence clause by clause and its results are recorded rather than claimed - the table's provenance is checkable (EXPECTED equals the run's base-table.json, captured with the base tree's module on stderr), the seven-file selection matches my own AST scan at both revisions, both basetemps are gone, and the failing-id sets are identical - but the head arm's log names the base revision on its header, so the revision in after_suite is not what that log testifies to.
justifications.fit: the change reuses the landed shared parser, keeps the module's private-helper idiom and per-reader policy docstrings, and carries no plan, ticket or author identifiers in code, comments or commit messages, though the test module's docstring names _manifest_wait twice where the sixth reader is _seconds_since_dispatch.
justifications.goal_fidelity: the six readers resolve through reckon._timestamps.parse_utc with zero fromisoformat calls left in reckon/crew/recovery.py under my own AST scan and grep, and my 16-input probe of two matched scratch trees reproduces all 36 recorded cells, but it also moves 11 of 96 cells on shapes the recorded table does not carry, so the "keeps its own policy" half of the goal holds only for the recorded inputs.
justifications.scope_discipline: the diff 25dabb31..e455cc075 touches exactly the three declared paths, and its nine hunks fall in the import line and the six named functions only, with the declared figures directory unused.
